# A remote call can outlive its window port, and `mounted` cannot tell the guards apart

## Context

Three separate sightings on 2026-09-15, all surfaced by `#18554`'s worker-error fixture rather than by any assertion, and all the same shape — **a remote call issued against a port whose window has already gone**:

1. `apps/colors` `updateGrid` destructuring a null `grid` after teardown;
2. `DockCrossWindowWitnessNL` — `Target worker 'cw-win-a' does not exist`;
3. `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL` — `no live port for destination "…" (remoteMethod Neo.main.DomAccess.getBoundingClientRect)` and the same for `Neo.main.addon.ResizeObserver.register`, plus `Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow: project() threw against a live owner`.

Individually each reads as a local race and gets patched locally. Together they name one missing distinction. The class was spotted by @neo-opus-grace across the three; the mechanism below is measured.

**This is not "add a `.catch`".** The engine already has the machinery; see *The Problem*.

## ⛔ Scope correction, 2026-09-15 — `NEO_DEAD_PORT` is ONE OF TWO teardown shapes

Found by `e2e-engine` on `#18743` and measured at `dev@e1f1d00307`. This body says *"four sites implement it correctly with an identical predicate"*. That predicate covers **one** of the two shapes this engine actually rejects with:

| shape | set at | already read by |
|---|---|---|
| `code: 'NEO_DEAD_PORT'` | `src/worker/Base.mjs:670` — no live port for a destination | the four sites named below |
| `name: 'PortDisconnectedError'` | `src/worker/Base.mjs:508` — port disconnected **mid-flight** | `src/Neo.mjs:1255,1266` · `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:388` · `src/worker/App.mjs:566` |

`worker/Base.mjs:508` does `Object.assign(new Error(…), {name: 'PortDisconnectedError'})` — **no `code` at all**. So four *other* sites already discriminate on the second shape and the predicate this ticket propagates does not.

**Consequence, measured on `#18743`:** the Gap-1 handlers added with that predicate reported eight `PortDisconnectedError` rejections into the page console — *a window closing mid-call*, which is the exact case this ticket exists to silence. `e2e/core/WorkerErrorGate.spec.mjs:76` caught it; the unit tier cannot, because its stub never disconnects a real port.

**So Gap 1 is not "copy the predicate to the sites that lack it."** It is: the predicate needs both shapes, and then the sites need it. That is also the case for extracting `isExpectedTeardown(reason)` onto `worker/Base.mjs` — six transcriptions exist and four of them never learned the second shape, which is what copies do.

## The Problem

`src/worker/Base.mjs:670` already types the condition, deliberately:

```js
// A window got closed and its message port no longer exists (SharedWorkers).
// Typed, so consumers can discriminate expected teardown from real failures
reject(Object.assign(new Error(`… no live port for destination "${dest}" …`), {code: 'NEO_DEAD_PORT'}))
```

So the design is **caller-side discrimination**, and four sites implement it correctly with an identical predicate — `src/table/Body.mjs:631`, `src/grid/Body.mjs:1287`, `src/draggable/DragZone.mjs:445`, `src/worker/Base.mjs:204`:

```js
reason !== Neo.isDestroyed && reason?.code !== 'NEO_DEAD_PORT' && console.error(…)
```

The sightings are the sites that do not. They split into **two gaps**, and only the first is mechanical.

**Gap 1 — no handler at all.** `src/manager/DomEvent.mjs:131`:

```js
ResizeObserver.register({componentId: component.id, id: targetId, windowId})
```

Fire-and-forget; the typed rejection becomes an unhandled App Worker rejection. `src/grid/Container.mjs:361` has the same shape.

**Gap 2 — the right instinct, the wrong predicate.** `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs:814` guards deliberately, and its comment explicitly refuses a blanket catch:

```js
// … a throw against a LIVE owner is a programming defect — surface it rather than swallow it
// silently (a blanket catch would hide real bugs behind a "just a teardown race" assumption).
if (owner.mounted) {
    console.error('Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow: project() threw against a live owner', error)
}
```

**That reasoning is correct and must not be weakened.** But the observed error is emitted from *inside* that `if`, so `owner.mounted` was `true` while the port was dead. The error is conditional on `owner.mounted`; it firing **is** the measurement.

**`mounted` is App-Worker state; the port belongs to a window.** A component stays `mounted` in the App Worker's model after the window hosting it has closed, so `owner.mounted` cannot separate *live owner* from *owner whose window closed* — exactly the distinction the guard reaches for. The predicate is one layer off the thing it tests.

That is why this is one ticket and not three patches: closing Gap 1 alone silences two sightings and leaves the guarded site still wrong.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/worker/Base.mjs:655-682` — `promiseMessage`, and the `NEO_DEAD_PORT` typing that already exists.
- `src/manager/DomEvent.mjs:121-132` — `addResizeObserver`, unhandled.
- `src/grid/Container.mjs:361` — same shape.
- `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs:809-821` — the deliberate guard whose predicate is one layer off.
- `src/core/Observable.mjs:156` — `Duplicate event handler attached`, which co-occurs across all three arms of the popup-over-popup spec and may share a root with re-registration after a retired window; **not assumed to be the same defect**.
- There is no predicate today that answers *"is this component's window still connected?"* at the App-Worker/port boundary. Whether that belongs on `manager.Window`, on the component, or as a `worker.Base` helper is the design question this ticket opens, not one it answers.

## The Fix

Attribution before repair; the two gaps have different answers.

1. Establish the liveness predicate — *is the window backing this component still connected?* — and decide its owning surface. This is the load-bearing step.
2. `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs:814` adopts it in place of `owner.mounted`, preserving the intent of its comment: a throw against a genuinely live owner must still surface.
3. Gap-1 sites (`manager/DomEvent.mjs:131`, `grid/Container.mjs:361`) take the established four-site predicate.
4. Re-run `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL` whole-file with the Brain runtime; `:585` is the arm that reaches teardown unconditionally.

## Decision Record impact

`none` — no ADR currently governs liveness at the App-Worker/window-port boundary. If step 1 lands a new shared predicate, that step should reassess whether it warrants one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — A liveness predicate exists that distinguishes *live owner* from *owner whose window has closed*, with its owning surface named and its choice justified against `manager.Window` / component / `worker.Base` alternatives.
- [ ] **AC-2** — `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs` uses it; a throw against a genuinely live owner still reports, shown by an arm that fails when the predicate is inverted.
- [ ] **AC-3** — `src/manager/DomEvent.mjs:131` and `src/grid/Container.mjs:361` discriminate `NEO_DEAD_PORT` using the same predicate as the four existing sites; a real failure at those sites still reports.
- [ ] **AC-4** — `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL`, whole-file with the Brain runtime wired and `--workers=1`, reports **zero** `no live port for destination` and zero `project() threw against a live owner`. Measured at `dev@6efce3e976`: 5 and 1 respectively, so this is a real state change and not a flake flip.

  > **AC-4 corrected 2026-09-15, after implementation, by its author.** It originally required the `:585` arm to *pass*. That conflated two defects, and the run proved them separable: the dead-port class went 5 → 0 and the Overflow false positive 1 → 0, while `Duplicate event handler attached` stayed at **7, unchanged** — the defect this ticket's Out of Scope already excluded as *"co-occurs, root not established"*. An arm-level pass is therefore not reachable from this ticket's own scope, and was never this ticket's to deliver. The arm's green lives on `#18731`'s AC-2, where the arm-level criteria are. **This is a correction of a mis-specified AC, not a bar lowered to match what shipped** — the new wording is strictly measurable and the delivered evidence is what falsifies or confirms it.
- [ ] **AC-5** — Red-first: each repair shown failing before and passing after, at one head.

## Out of Scope

- The resize-clamp defect in the same spec — `#18731`, already fixed on `agent/18731-resize-headroom`; that fix is what unmasked this by letting two more arms reach teardown.
- `Duplicate event handler attached` — co-occurs, root not established. Dispositioned here rather than assumed: if step 1 does not resolve it, it needs its own attribution.
- Changing `mounted`'s own semantics. It has consumers throughout the engine; this ticket adds a distinction rather than redefining an existing one.

## AC-1: the predicate already exists, and the ticket gets smaller

Claimed and started. AC-1 asked for a liveness predicate to be *established* and its owning surface *chosen*. It does not need designing — `worker.Base` already has one, purpose-built, and its docblock names the exact distinction the `Overflow` guard is reaching for.

### Why a window-registry predicate cannot work — the ordering

`src/worker/Base.mjs#onDisconnect`:

```js
sourcePort.appNames.size || me.removePort(sourcePort)   // the port dies here
…
this.fire('disconnect', {appName, windowId})            // every subscriber hears AFTER
```

The port is retired **first**; the `disconnect` event fires after. So everything downstream of that event — including `manager.Window`'s `onWindowDisconnect` → `unregister` — is strictly later than the moment `promiseMessage` starts rejecting. **Any registry updated by the event is stale by construction inside exactly the interval where these errors fire.** That rules out `manager.Window.get(windowId)`, which was my first candidate.

It also explains the observed symptom without appeal to timing luck: `owner.mounted` is true, the window registry still resolves, and the port is already gone.

### The predicate that is current at the right instant

`departedWindowIds`, written **inside `removePort`** — same bookkeeping, same moment, no staleness window:

```js
/**
 * Only needed for SharedWorkers: the windows whose port this worker retired, newest last and capped at 16, so a
 * reply that can no longer reach one of them reads as that window's departure rather than a lost reply.
 */
departedWindowIds = null
```

*"…reads as that window's departure rather than a lost reply"* is the Overflow guard's question, already answered. And `removePort:485` already computes `windowGone` internally for its own purposes.

So the shape is `Neo.currentWorker.departedWindowIds.has(windowId)`, and the owning surface is `worker.Base` — beside the port table `promiseMessage` itself consults, which is the only registry that cannot disagree with it.

### Two properties a naive implementation would get wrong, both checked

| candidate | why it fails |
|---|---|
| `manager.Window.get(windowId)` | updated by the `disconnect` event, i.e. after `removePort` — stale in the exact interval |
| `Neo.currentWorker.getPort({windowId})` | `ports` is initialised to `[]` **unconditionally**, not only for SharedWorkers — so in dedicated-worker mode it returns `null` for every window and reports them all dead. A false negative, not a crash. I checked this after first reading the `ports = null` field declaration and getting it backwards. |

`departedWindowIds` is also initialised unconditionally, so `.has()` is safe in dedicated mode and correctly returns `false` — where a dead port genuinely does mean something other than a departed window.

**Bounded, and worth stating:** the Set is an LRU capped at 16. That is correct for *"did this call just fail because its window went?"* — a recency question — and would be wrong for *"has this window ever departed?"* Any consumer must ask the first question.

### What this does to the ticket

AC-1 narrows from *design a predicate and justify its surface* to *adopt the existing one*. The remaining work is unchanged and is where the care goes: `Overflow` swapping `owner.mounted` for it **without weakening its intent** — a throw against a genuinely live owner must still surface — plus the two unguarded sites, and the red-first pairing on `:585`.

Not touching `mounted`'s semantics, as scoped.

⚖️ **Ada** · `@neo-opus-ada` · Claude Opus 5 · Claude Code

## AC-3 retracted by its author — @tobiu's RC, and the measurement backs him

**AC-3 required `src/manager/DomEvent.mjs` and `src/grid/Container.mjs` to discriminate `NEO_DEAD_PORT`. I am retracting it, and the two edits it justified are reverted to `dev` verbatim** (`d7e04edb21`).

**The premise was false.** I wrote that AC believing those two sites were *defective* for calling fire-and-forget without a handler. Measured across the engine:

```
main-thread addon call sites (Neo.main.addon.X.y) : 89
…across distinct addons                           : 38
…that attach a .catch                             : 0
```

They are not defective. **They are consistent with 87 others**, and my change made 2 of 89 special.

**Worse, the two were not chosen on merit.** They are the sites that happened to surface in `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL`, a spec that mass-destroys windows. @tobiu's objection is exact:

> *you can not say "grid resizeobserver register differently" than 25+ other main thread addons and vast amounts of cross thread calls do. only because you do mass destruction inside playwright tests.*

An engine change derived from a harness artifact, applied at the wrong layer. If unhandled teardown rejections are worth handling, they are worth handling at the **one boundary all 89 calls pass through** — `promiseMessage` / the remote proxy — not at two consumers someone tripped over. That is a design decision about the cross-thread call contract, and it is not mine to smuggle in as a patch to two files.

`isExpectedTeardown()` is removed with them: it had no other consumer, and an engine method nothing calls is accretion.

### What survives, and why it is not the same class

`tab/plugin/Overflow` stays. That defect needs no harness to exist: `owner.mounted` is App-Worker state, a component **stays mounted after its window closes**, so the guard reported *every* cross-window teardown as a programming defect. Console noise in any real multi-window application, and the guard's own comment says it is meant to distinguish exactly that. `isWindowDeparted()` is the predicate it needs and its only consumer.

Measured on the arm: `Overflow: project() threw against a live owner` goes **1 → 0**.

### Corrected AC-3

- [x] **AC-3 (retracted)** — the two call sites are consistent with 87 other addon call sites and need no change. Whether the cross-thread call contract should handle teardown rejections **at the boundary** is a real question, unowned, and deliberately not answered here.

**This is the second AC I have had to correct on my own ticket today**, and the two failures are different: AC-4 conflated two defects, this one asserted a defect that measurement says is normal practice. Both were written before the evidence. The reusable form: **before calling a call site defective, count how many siblings do the same thing.** One `grep -c` would have prevented this.

⚖️ **Ada** · `@neo-opus-ada` · Claude Opus 5 · Claude Code
